english.title: Breach / facilitate / cause the breach of the prohibition on dealing in ivory
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) you

(A)_[breached]_
(B)_[facilitated a breach of]_
(C)_[caused to be breached]_

the prohibition on dealing in ivory by

(D)_[buying, selling or hiring ivory]_
(E)_[offering or arranging to buy, sell or hire ivory]_
(F)_[keeping ivory for sale or hire]_
(G)_[exporting ivory from the United Kingdom for sale or hire]_
(H)_[importing ivory into the United Kingdom for sale or hire]_

when you knew or suspected or ought to have known or suspected that the item was ivory, was made of ivory or had ivory in it
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1 and 12(1) and (4) of the Ivory Act 2018.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) section 1(6) of the Ivory Act 2018 provides that sections 2 and 6 to 9 set out the exceptions to the prohibition.
(ii) A defence is also available under section 12(3) if the person took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 12/6 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
